meta.subtitle: Security that keeps its head above water
meta.purpose: This guide shows how to present the Halyard brand consistently. It is for employees, agencies, partners, and AI design tools. The rules are fixed; creativity inside them is encouraged.
meta.audience: Marketing, sales, product, agencies, and partners producing anything with our name on it.

foundation.mission: Give every security team the calm, clear signal they need to act.
foundation.vision: A world where security teams spend their time deciding, not searching.
foundation.positioning: Halyard is the detection platform that turns noisy telemetry into a short, ranked list of what matters, so lean security teams act first and explain later.
foundation.boilerplate: Halyard helps security teams cut through alert noise. The Halyard platform correlates signals across cloud, identity, and endpoint to surface the handful of threats that matter, ranked and explained. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Denver, Colorado, Halyard protects more than 400 organizations. Learn more at halyard.example.

pillars.name: Clarity
pillars.description: We say the useful thing first.
points: No dashboards for their own sake

foundation.direction: Over the next two years we are moving from a detection tool to the system of record for security decisions. The brand should feel more like a trusted instrument than a startup.

voice.summary: We sound like the most senior analyst on the team: direct, unhurried, and specific.
tone_notes: Lead with the outcome, then the evidence
Cite a source for every number
Never use breach headlines to sell

logos.description: The Halyard logo pairs the Signal mark, a wave rising inside a circle, with our wordmark. The two always appear together in the approved relationship.
anatomy: Signal mark: the circle and wave
The mark and wordmark are one lockup and are never redrawn

variants.name: Full color
variants.usage: Default. White and light gray backgrounds.

variants.name: Signal mark
variants.usage: Favicons and avatars where the full logo will not fit.

clear_space.unit_description: half the height of the Signal mark
clear_space.rule: Keep a clear zone of x on every side of the logo, where x is half the height of the Signal mark. No text, imagery, or edges inside it.
clear_space.small_size_rule: At favicon sizes the mark may fill up to 90% of the canvas.

where_not: Next to breach news imagery or hacker stock photos
In a partner's product UI without a signed agreement
donts_custom: Do not use the Signal mark as a bullet point or decorative icon
Do not animate the wave without the approved motion file

cobranding.intro: When Halyard appears with a partner, both brands should look like equals.

rules.title: Order
rules.text: Halyard first in Halyard-led materials; partner first in theirs.

rules.title: Balance
rules.text: Match visual weight, not pixel width.

rules.title: Mode
rules.text: Both logos in the same mode.

donts: Do not convert the Halyard logo to grayscale to match a partner
Do not give either logo visual dominance
Do not create a combined lockup

groups.name: Primary
groups.usage: Halyard Blue and Ink carry the brand. Use them for logo, headlines, and large color fields.

groups.name: Accent
groups.usage: Use sparingly for calls to action, highlights, and charts. Never as a background behind body text.

groups.name: Neutrals
groups.usage: Structure: backgrounds, borders, dividers, tables, and body copy.

colors.gradient_rules: One gradient only, Halyard Blue to Ink, at 135 degrees. Use for hero backgrounds, never behind small text.
donts: Do not tint or shade brand colors outside the defined neutrals
Do not set body text in Signal Coral
Do not place Halyard Blue text on Ink

families.name: Inter
families.usage: Body copy, UI, tables, and captions.

rules: Headlines in Ink, White, or Halyard Blue only
donts: Use more than two weights in one layout
Set body copy below 14 px on screen

photography.summary: Real practitioners at work, in natural light.
dont: Hooded hackers or green code rain

name_usage: Halyard, never HALYARD or Halyard Labs
The Halyard platform on first reference, then Halyard
Do not add 'Halyard' in front of feature names
formatting: Never use & or + in place of 'and' in body copy
